QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_21

question.text: A close-ended Cat III fund has total paid-in capital of INR 100 crore and has distributed a cumulative INR 145 crore to investors over the fund life. What is the DPI?

explanation.text: The Logic: DPI = Total Distributions / Paid-in Capital = 145 / 100 = 1.45x. DPI > 1 means investors have received back more than they invested. For Cat III (open-ended with daily NAV) DPI is LESS relevant than HWM/TWR — this is a Cat I/II primary metric. The Trap: 0.69 inverts. 1.00 is breakeven. 2.45 adds 1. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D Cat I/II Manager uses DPI as a primary metric. XIX-E (Cat III) flags it as less relevant for open-ended funds — HWM/TWR dominate. Manager's Pro-Tip: For a close-ended Cat III fund in wind-down, DPI is useful; for an open-ended Cat III with daily dealing, use rolling TWR and MWR instead. Don't mis-report DPI for a perpetual fund.
